summary: Learn AI for MEAL through targeting, early warning, data pipelines, and safeguards. Build practical workflows with ODK, KoboToolbox, and DHIS2.
lede: AI and predictive analytics in MEAL apply programme data to evaluation, targeting, early-warning, and feedback workflows. For MEAL and social protection professionals, the course covers preparing indicator data, assessing predictive outputs, and designing accountable workflows. Participants practise data-quality checks, risk-signal review, feedback triage, and human oversight while considering uncertainty, bias, and when rule-based methods are safer.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who connect programme evidence, humanitarian decisions, social protection delivery, and responsible technology. It suits beginner to intermediate AI users who already work with MEAL processes and want enough technical fluency to commission, assess, or design AI-supported workflows without becoming machine learning engineers.
prerequisites: You should have working experience with MEAL, programme monitoring, humanitarian data, social protection delivery, or a related evidence function. Familiarity with spreadsheets and at least one data collection or reporting platform, such as ODK, KoboToolbox, or DHIS2, will help. No coding or programming is required for completion. Advanced machine learning, model engineering, and production deployment are introduced at conceptual awareness level, while workflow design, data review, governance mapping, and reporting receive operational application. Bring a laptop if possible. TrainingCred can provide representative datasets and digital templates for exercises; access to organizational data is optional and should follow your internal safeguarding and privacy controls.
